name: frontend-oracle-design-lifecycle-forward-v1
purpose: Forward scenarios for adaptive lifecycle planning. Assertions are semantic reviewer prompts, not an executable runtime grader.

cases.prompt: Change an already-approved label in one existing button. Do not alter behavior, layout, state, or API.
expectedConstraints: Keep the Low single-node fast path
forbiddenConstraints: Do not invent an Oracle card, lifecycle plan, milestone, or review ceremony
semanticAssertions: The response preserves the Low path and explains why lifecycle-adaptation is not loaded

cases.prompt: Design a new medium-risk filter panel for a greenfield screen. The product has not decided whether filter changes apply immediately or only after pressing Apply. Produce the first Draft Oracle, without implementing it.
expectedConstraints: Keep the unresolved apply-policy as an Open question
forbiddenConstraints: Do not invent lifecycle ceremony or reverse-engineer an existing system
Do not claim implementation, approval, lock, or executed evidence
Do not load lifecycle-adaptation solely because product policy is unresolved
semanticAssertions: The reviewer can distinguish a product-policy decision from a technical implementation choice

cases.prompt: In an existing checkout, the current code allows retry after a failed address save, while the approved legal note says the form must require re-validation. Map the change impact and prepare a Draft Oracle; do not resolve the conflict by copying the code.
expectedConstraints: Record the affected ownership and validation boundary
forbiddenConstraints: Do not treat current implementation as policy
Do not lock or implement while sources conflict
semanticAssertions: The reviewer verifies that brownfield impact mapping does not silently promote code behavior to product policy

cases.prompt: Fix a small high-risk permission check in an existing admin form. The requested patch is only three lines. Deliver it through the Oracle workflow and prove the denied request; do not skip VALID_RED or independent review because the diff is small.
expectedConstraints: Await the existing approval/confirmation gate before claiming delivery
forbiddenConstraints: Do not waive RED or review based on line count
Do not claim executed evidence or REVIEW_VERIFIED without approval and delivery
Do not load lifecycle-adaptation solely because risk is High or the patch is small
semanticAssertions: The reviewer checks risk-driven minimum guarantees separately from investigation depth

cases.prompt: Plan a medium-risk order editor with two milestones: optimistic row updates and background save retry. Both touch the same cache and can reorder notifications. Decide whether they form one independently verifiable result or must remain grouped.
expectedConstraints: Evaluate milestone boundaries by independently verifiable outcomes
Treat shared cache and notification side effects as a grouping concern
forbiddenConstraints: Do not split units merely by component or folder
Do not claim independent parallel completion without an integration contract
semanticAssertions: The reviewer can see why shared side effects constrain unit boundaries

cases.prompt: Implement three unrelated dashboard widgets as three separate Oracle cards and automatically report one aggregate completion when all cards are green. Propose the safest lifecycle handling, noting any unsupported coordination.
expectedConstraints: State that multi-card aggregate coordination is not supported by this update
Keep each card's existing approval and verification contract
forbiddenConstraints: Do not invent a scheduler, aggregate ledger, or cross-card completion state
semanticAssertions: The reviewer distinguishes a bounded unsupported feature from a silently invented orchestration layer
